properties.decision:
RECORDED AS A FINDING PLUS AN OPEN QUESTION, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Found 2026-08-04 IMMEDIATELY AFTER accepting `dec:coord-board-in-graph`, while updating AGENTS.md to match the move — by noticing that a sentence in it had silently become false. Nothing here is settled, and this does NOT reverse the move.

THE COLLISION, BETWEEN TWO RULES THAT ARE EACH CORRECT ALONE. (1) `dec:export-once-per-pr` and AGENTS.md: "a branch may hold as many commits as you like; only one of them may touch `docs/design/reflow2.json`, and it should be the LAST" — because PRs squash-merge, so only the final export's `prev_content_hash` survives and an intermediate export puts a hole in the lineage chain. (2) `dec:coord-board-in-graph`, accepted minutes earlier: a claim is graph state, recorded by `claim_region`, and it travels in the committed export. TOGETHER THEY SAY: A CLAIM MADE BEFORE THE WORK BECOMES VISIBLE TO ANYONE ELSE ONLY WHEN THE PR MERGES — which is after the work is finished. Claiming first is exactly what a claim is for.

⭐ THIS FALSIFIES A CLAIM MADE ON THE DECIDING NODE, AND THE CORRECTION BELONGS ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN BEING QUIETLY ABSORBED. `dec:coord-board-in-graph` argued, both while open and at acceptance: "both travel in the committed export exactly as COORD.md travels in git — so VISIBILITY IS UNCHANGED." That is wrong, and the asymmetry is precisely the one that matters. COORD.md could be committed and pushed AS ITS OWN COMMIT the moment work started — AGENTS.md even prescribed it ("put the COORD claim commit, which carries no export, FIRST"). The export cannot be, because writing it early is the thing that breaks the lineage chain. The old advice was not merely superseded; the property it depended on — that a claim costs no export — is the property the move removed.

WHAT IT COSTS TODAY: NOTHING, AND THAT IS WHY THE MOVE STANDS. reflow2 has one writer. `dec:coord-board-in-graph` already records that the claims layer is "UNPROVEN under contention" and that the single-writer proof is all that was obtained. This is a second, sharper instance of that same limit — and it is worse than the general statement, because it is not that contention is untested but that a KNOWN MECHANISM makes pre-announcement impossible.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) ACCEPT IT AND SAY SO — with one writer a claim is a note to your future self, and the export at PR time is soon enough. Cheapest and honest; the counter is that it silently retires "claim before you work", which is the discipline the board existed to enforce. (b) LET A CLAIM COMMIT EXPORT, AND EXEMPT IT FROM THE CHAIN — the export gate would need to distinguish a claims-only delta from a design delta. Counter: the gate exists because silent chain breaks happened repeatedly ([BL-107], six commits in a row; [BL-156]), and an exemption is a hole in exactly the check that catches them. (c) CLAIMS LEAVE THE EXPORT — a separate small committed file, written per claim, merged by union like COORD.md was. Counter: that is COORD.md with extra steps, and re-splits the fact into two places, which is the failure the move existed to end. (d) PUBLISH CLAIMS OUT OF BAND — a hosted surface or live tier, which `dec:central-host` and `dec:live-tier` both already ask about. Counter: both are open, both are much larger than this, and `dec:multi-writer-architecture` settled on the repo file with no hosted service.

WHAT MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED: that COORD.md's `merge=union` in `.gitattributes` is what made the old claim commit cheap and conflict-free, and that `docs/design/reflow2.json` uses the `merge=reflow2` three-way driver instead — the two files were never merging the same way, and any option here inherits that difference.

NOT CHECKED: whether `release_claim` has the same problem in reverse — a claim released mid-branch is also invisible until the PR merges, which would mean a finished lane still reads as held by exactly the mechanism that was supposed to fix stale claims. Liveness would cover the case where the session ended, but not the case where the same session released and kept working.
properties.name: OPEN — a claim in the graph cannot be announced before the work, because the export it rides in may only be written once per PR
properties.rationale:
Filed the moment it was found rather than after, because it was found by the cheapest possible route — updating a document to match a decision, and noticing that one sentence in it had become false — and that route only exists while the change is being made. An hour later the sentence would have read as merely stale.

Recorded as its own node rather than as an amendment to `dec:coord-board-in-graph` because that decision is ACCEPTED and this does not reopen it: the move was right, one of its supporting arguments was wrong, and those are different facts. Folding a falsification into an accepted node would either weaken a decision that should stand or hide the correction — `dec:reopen-supersedes` sets the rule that a settled choice is not un-accepted, and this is not a re-opening.

The unchecked item about `release_claim` is named so its absence reads as a hole rather than as completed analysis — and it is the more alarming half, since it would undo the stale-claim fix that was the whole justification for the move.
